info.title: Understanding G-Factor
info.intro: <link>G-factor (load factor)</link> represents the vertical load experienced during flight:
info.normal: 1.0 G: Normal gravity (straight and level flight)
info.method:
This analysis combines vertical acceleration (from altitude changes) and lateral acceleration (from turning).

Always respect your wing's certified G-limits (8G during 3 seconds for EN 926-1).

gFactorTab.statsHelp: Confused about median, average, variance and deviation? <link>Check this out!</link>

coaching.centeringWidened: Circles widened from {r25} (p25) to {r75} (p75) around a {core} core: the lift narrowed at altitude. Try tightening as you climb.
coaching.centeringOrbit: You orbited {dist} from a {core} core (mean distance ~{ratio}× core radius). Try tighter turns when you feel the strongest lift.
coaching.centeringExcellent: Excellent centring: you stayed within {dist} of a {core} core.
coaching.slowCoreEntry: Slow core entry: {seconds} s ({pct}% of the climb) before reaching strongest lift. Consider wider initial circles to feel the gradient.
coaching.greatCoreEntry: Great core entry: found the strongest lift in {seconds} s.
coaching.lowEfficiency: Low efficiency: {gain} gain for {drift} of drift ({pct}%) in {wind} wind. Try tighter turns to stay over the lift.
coaching.goodEfficiency: Good efficiency: {gain} gain with only {drift} of drift ({pct}%).
coaching.variabilityPoorCentering: High variability (±{variability}) with circle radius spanning {r25} to {r75}. Likely poor centring rather than a turbulent thermal.
coaching.variabilityTurbulentCircling: High variability (±{variability}) with consistent {r25} to {r75} circling. Turbulent thermal.
coaching.smoothClimbAirspeed: Smooth, consistent climb (±{variability}) at {airspeed} airspeed. Well done!
coaching.flatBank: Flat bank ({bank}°) in a tight {core} core: try ~25° to keep your turn radius matched to the lift zone.
coaching.steepBank: Steep bank ({bank}°) in a wide {core} thermal: easing off would conserve airspeed and reduce sink rate.
coaching.solidWork: Solid thermal work: {gain} gained with {pct}% efficiency.
coaching.flightSummary: Across {count} thermals: median centring {median}%, with {excellent} excellent and {poor} below 50%.
coaching.flightSlowEntry: Slow core entry on {count} thermals (>50% of climb spent finding the core). Try wider initial circles to feel the gradient.
coaching.flightFlatBank: Bank stayed flat (<20°) in {count} tight cores: try ~25° to keep your turn radius matched to the lift zone.
coaching.flightBestClimb: Best climb: T#{index} at {time}, {gain} gain, {pct}% centring, {maxClimb} sustained. Excellent work.
coaching.flightWorstClimb: Worth reviewing: T#{index} at {time}, orbited {dist} from a {core} core ({pct}% centring). Try tighter turns when you feel the strongest lift.

thermalTimeAltitude.amslTitle: Above mean sea level (raw GPS altitude)
thermalTimeAltitude.caption: The dashed line is the day's working ceiling: how high your climbs typically topped out (median exit altitude of climbs gaining 100 m or more). When the line splits into two steps, the morning and afternoon ceilings differed. A step up usually means an inversion broke through, a step down usually means late-day decay.

lede.measuredHigh: Measured second by second over {minutes} min of flight, and the direction held tight (±{spread}°).
lede.measuredSwing: Measured second by second over {minutes} min of flight. The direction swung ±{spread}°. That's the air itself shifting, not estimation noise.
lede.noData: Wind is derived from ground-track residuals during thermalling. This flight didn't include enough qualifying thermals to fit a model.
lede.low: Wind direction scattered ±{spread}° across {count, plural, one {# thermal sample} other {# thermal samples}}. Take direction estimates with care; speed estimates are tighter.
lede.medium: Direction agreed within ±{spread}° across {count, plural, one {# thermal sample} other {# thermal samples}}. Solid enough to plan around, but worth a sanity-check against soundings.
lede.high: Direction held tight (±{spread}° across {count, plural, one {# thermal sample} other {# thermal samples}}). The wind read consistent through the climbing band.

hero.readings: {count, plural, one {# reading} other {# readings}} · 1 Hz

conditions.meanTooltip: Average of all values. Sensitive to outliers and extreme readings.
conditions.medianTooltip: Middle value when sorted. More robust than the mean when data is skewed.
conditions.stdDevTooltip: Standard deviation: how spread out the values are around the mean. Lower means more consistent.
conditions.percentile10Tooltip: Nine readings in ten were stronger than this. Steadier than a raw minimum, which a single sensor dropout can pin to zero.

windTab.empty: Not enough thermal data to estimate wind conditions for this flight.

heatmap.title: Wind speed by altitude through the flight
heatmap.ledeMeasured: Each circle averages a slice of the Vector Vario's per-second wind readings. The interpolated field shows where the air was working harder; hover anywhere for the speed.
heatmap.ledeEstimated: Each circle is a thermal where wind was estimated. The interpolated field shows where the air was working harder; hover any thermal for direction & speed.

direction.title: Where the air came from
direction.ledeRose: The orange pointer marks the aggregate bearing; the lavender arc shows scatter; coloured dots place each altitude band on the rose. Dot radius from centre encodes wind speed.
direction.ledeSingleBand: Only one altitude band was sampled. The pointer marks the aggregate bearing.
